vscode.guided.environments-add.consequen: Each name gets a .env.<name> file, a build:<name> task and an output folder. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.environments-add.project.t: MonoSmith: add environments (1/2): which web app?
vscode.guided.environments-add.names.tit: MonoSmith: add environments (2/2): the names to add
vscode.guided.environments-add.names.pro: Lowercase words, separated by commas. Edit the names, or write your own (such as qa, stage).
vscode.guided.environments-add.names.inv: Use lowercase words separated by commas, for example qa, stage.
vscode.guided.environments-remove.conseq: The .env.<name> files stay, because they hold your values. The default environment cannot be removed.
vscode.guided.environments-remove.projec: MonoSmith: remove environments (1/2): which web app?
vscode.guided.cache-repair.consequence: It deletes corrupt blobs, the entries that name them, unused blobs and leftover files. The next run of an affected task is slower.
vscode.guided.cache-prune.consequence: It removes the least recently used entries.
vscode.guided.cache-clear.consequence: It deletes the local cache. The remote cache stays, and the next run of every task is slower.
vscode.guided.why-miss.task.title: MonoSmith: why would a task run again?
vscode.guided.why-miss.task.prompt: The project and the task, as project:task.
vscode.guided.pipeline.consequence: The file is yours from then on: smith upgrade never rewrites it. An existing file is kept.
vscode.guided.pipeline.template.title: MonoSmith: add a pipeline (1/2): which one?
vscode.guided.pipeline.project.title: MonoSmith: add a pipeline (2/2): which app does it build?
vscode.guided.pipeline.project.prompt: Only a deploy pipeline builds an app. Enter leaves it out.
vscode.guided.tauri-icon.consequence: It overwrites the icons the plan lists.
vscode.guided.tauri-icon.logo.title: MonoSmith: the square PNG the icons are made from
vscode.guided.tauri-icon.project.title: MonoSmith: which app?
vscode.guided.tauri-icon.project.prompt: Only when more than one project has a src-tauri. Enter leaves it out.
vscode.guided.docker-description.consequ: It calls Docker Hub with your login and replaces the description of each app's image. "Docker Hub Descriptions: Name the Repositories" shows which ones without calling it.
vscode.guided.mcp-install.consequence: It writes the file that lets the assistant start smith's MCP server. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.mcp-install.tools.title: MonoSmith: which assistants?
vscode.guided.tauri-add.consequence: It writes src-tauri and the tauri tasks in the app. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.tauri-add.project.title: MonoSmith: Tauri (1/2): which app?
vscode.guided.tauri-add.project.prompt: The name of a web app of the workspace.
vscode.guided.tauri-add.identifier.title: MonoSmith: Tauri (2/2): the bundle identifier
vscode.guided.tauri-add.identifier.promp: Like com.yourcompany.yourapp. Enter takes com.<workspace>.<project>, which is the default.
vscode.guided.plugin-install.consequence: smith checks the archive against its SHA-256 and installs it in .smith/plugins. The plugin is never started by the install. A plugin runs with your privileges and smith does not sandbox it: read it before you trust it. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.plugin-install.term.title: MonoSmith: install a plugin (1/3): search the marketplace
vscode.guided.plugin-install.term.prompt: Words of the name, description, roles or languages. Enter lists them all.
vscode.guided.plugin-install.plugin.titl: MonoSmith: install a plugin (2/3): which one?
vscode.guided.plugin-install.trust.title: MonoSmith: install a plugin (3/3): do you trust it?
vscode.guided.plugin-install.trust.pinne: it may run at once; smith writes the SHA-256 of its program to smith.toml, and CI refuses a changed file
vscode.guided.ci-generate.consequence: It rewrites the generated pipeline files; the plan shows a diff of each. A pipeline of your own (smith pipeline) is not touched. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.derive-update.consequence: It rewrites the files that follow from the project graph. A file you edited is reported, not overwritten. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.config-set.consequence: It edits smith.toml and nothing else. Nothing is committed: review it with git.
vscode.guided.config-set.setting.title: MonoSmith: change a setting (1/2): which one?
vscode.guided.config-set.value.title: MonoSmith: change a setting (2/2): the new value
vscode.guided.config-unset.consequence: It removes the line from smith.toml, so the setting takes its default again. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.config-unset.setting.title: MonoSmith: reset a setting: which one?
vscode.guided.plugin-enable.consequence: It edits smith.toml. The projects the plugin discovers appear in smith. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.plugin-enable.plugin.title: MonoSmith: turn a plugin on
vscode.guided.plugin-disable.consequence: It edits smith.toml. The projects this plugin discovers disappear from smith until you turn it on again; smith names them after the change. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.architecture.consequence: It edits the lines of smith.toml that turn an architecture on, and nothing else. An architecture that applies to none of your projects checks nothing: smith warns. "none" turns the checks off. Nothing is committed.
vscode.guided.architecture.choice.title: MonoSmith: the architecture of the workspace
vscode.guided.architecture.choice.placeh: The one in use is marked
